description.narrative: Due to war in Gaza more than 80% of WASH infrastructures are damaged and is facing a severe crisis, the water production has been reduced to 22% of pre-war levels. Many water facilities, especially in Gaza City and Northern Gaza, are non-operational, leaving hundreds of thousands without reliable access to waterIn July 2024, Oxfam published the report “Water War Crimes,” which indicated that in Gaza City, 100% of municipal desalination plants and seawater desalination plants, 88% of water wells, and 89% of water storage reservoirs have been destroyed or rendered non-operational. Based on the Gaza Rapid WASH assessment report from October 2024, more than half of assessed households (64.2%) reported receiving less than 6 liters per person per day (LPPD) ofdrinking and cooking water,while almost half (46.4%) received less than 9 LPPD of domestic water. The hard-to-reach areas in Northern governorates were the worst affected, receiving as little as 2 LPPD of drinking water and 5.1 LPPD of domestic water.Access to safe water is further hindered by storage and infrastructure issues, including insufficient water points and a lack of containers for storage. Water treatment and quality testing remain significant challenges, as insufficient chlorination and contamination with pathogens, such as E. coli and fecal coliforms, exacerbate health risks for Gaza’s residents. The December 2024 Water Quality Surveillance report indicates that out of 306 water samples taken from production, distribution, and user points, 79% were non-compliant for Free Residual Chlorine, and 72.8% of the samples collected for drinking water did not meet agreed standards.A recent ceasefire presents a long-awaited opportunity for millions of displaced people to return to their places of origin after being displaced multiple times over the past 15 months. it also brings significant opportunity, in restoring WASH services and ensuring access to safe water and to complement other ongoing actions (food, Health, protection, shelter) for Gaza's residents.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
